summary.text: Maria Elvira Salazar is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 27th District. A Miami native and the daughter of Cuban exiles, she spent decades as a Spanish-language television journalist before losing the 2018 race for the seat, winning it in 2020 and taking office in 2021. She is seeking a third re-election.

paragraphs.text: Salazar was born in Miami in 1961; her official biography says she was born in Little Havana, the daughter of Cuban exiles.
She studied at the Deerborne School of Coral Gables and graduated from Miami Dade College, according to her official biography.
She earned a bachelor's degree in communications from the University of Miami in 1983 and a master's in public administration from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government in 1995.
Salazar worked as a television journalist, reporter and news anchor, starting at age 22.
Her official biography lists Telemundo, Univision, AmericaTeve, MegaTV and CNN en Español, and says she is a five-time Emmy Award winner who interviewed Fidel Castro.
Salazar ran for the 27th District in 2018 and lost the general election. She ran again in 2020, defeated incumbent Donna Shalala, and took office in 2021; she won re-election in 2022.
She serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Small Business Committee, and she chaired the Foreign Affairs Western Hemisphere subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress.
Salazar lives in Coral Gables with her two daughters, according to her official biography.
